application_policy: DO NOT apply to the production engine merely because the defects are obvious. This is an engine-wide behavioural change affecting stock content, CI and any tooling that shells ImportAssets. It requires its own review, a stock-map regression pass, and a decision about whether to carry it as a local patch.

changes.behavior_before: ImportAndSave returning false logs 'Could not import all groups' but the commandlet still exits 0.
changes.behavior_after: Result is set to a nonzero error code when ImportAndSave returns false, so CI and orchestrators can gate on exit status.
changes.stock_map_compatibility_risk: HIGH. Any existing pipeline that invokes ImportAssets in a situation the engine currently reports as failure while still producing acceptable output would start failing. Must be surveyed before rollout.
changes.test_case: Feed a settings file whose single group fails to import; assert nonzero exit and the existing error log line.

changes.defect: ParseImportSettings bSuccess is never assigned true
changes.evidence: line 119 'bool bSuccess = false;' ; line 167 'return bSuccess;' ; no assignment anywhere in the function
changes.behavior_before: The function always returns false, including on a fully successful parse. Main discards the value at line 429, so the bug is currently latent.
changes.behavior_after: bSuccess is set true when the file loads, the JSON deserializes, and at least one group passes JsonObjectToUStruct plus Data->IsValid(). Once P4 lands, this becomes load-bearing.
changes.stock_map_compatibility_risk: LOW in isolation, because the return value is unused today.
changes.test_case: Valid settings file with 20 valid groups returns true; a missing file and a malformed JSON both return false.

changes.evidence: line 170-172 SavePackage returns GEditor->SavePackage(...); line 301 'SavePackage(PackageToSave, PackageFilename);' with the result unused
changes.behavior_before: A failed package write is invisible; bImportAndSaveSucceeded stays true.
changes.behavior_after: Capture the bool; on false set bImportAndSaveSucceeded = false and emit an explicit error naming the package filename.
changes.stock_map_compatibility_risk: MEDIUM. Read-only or source-control-locked packages that currently fail silently would now be reported. That is the intent, but it will surface latent failures in existing pipelines.
changes.test_case: Save into a read-only or unwritable destination; assert the failure is reported and, with P1, that the exit is nonzero.

changes.defect: ParseImportSettings return value is discarded by the caller
changes.evidence: line 429 'ParseImportSettings(ImportSettingsPath);' with no assignment or check
changes.behavior_after: Check the result; on false, log the parse diagnostics and return nonzero without calling ImportAndSave, so a settings file that was never consumed can never be mistaken for an empty-but-successful import.
changes.behavior_before: A missing or invalid settings file leaves ImportDataList empty, ImportAndSave iterates zero times, returns true, and the commandlet exits 0 having done nothing.
changes.stock_map_compatibility_risk: LOW to MEDIUM. The only workflows affected are ones that pass a bad settings path and currently succeed silently.
changes.test_case: Point -importSettings at a nonexistent file and at malformed JSON; assert nonzero exit in both cases.

changes.defect: Zero-output import is indistinguishable from success
changes.evidence: line 213-214 'if(ImportedAssets.Num() > 0 && bImportAndSaveSucceeded)' gates the entire save block
changes.behavior_before: If the import performs substantial FBX/DDC work and yields zero UObjects, nothing is dirtied, nothing is saved, and exit is 0.
changes.behavior_after: When a non-empty requested import yields ImportedAssets.Num() == 0, treat it as a failure. This must be conditional on the request being non-empty, to avoid breaking legitimate empty or no-op invocations.
changes.stock_map_compatibility_risk: HIGH and needs source-contract analysis first. See the open question below.
changes.test_case: Settings requesting one FBX whose import yields no assets; assert nonzero exit.

open_question_before_P5: It is NOT established that no legitimate UE 4.26 workflow intentionally invokes ImportAssets with a non-empty request expecting zero ImportedAssets. Before changing P5, survey the engine and project call sites for invocations that rely on a zero result, and confirm whether an empty ImportGroups array with a valid file is used as an intentional no-op. If such workflows exist, P5 must be scoped to 'request non-empty AND produced zero' and must not reject an explicitly empty request.
recommended_sequencing: P2 and P4 first: they are latent, low risk, and make the settings path trustworthy.
P3 next: it converts silent save failures into reported ones.
P1 last among the reporting fixes, because it is the one that changes externally visible exit codes.
P5 only after the open question is answered.
relationship_to_wrapper_contract: These engine changes are strictly better than a wrapper gate but are not a substitute for one. The wrapper contract in reports/IMPORT_SUCCESS_CONTRACT_V2.json depends on no engine modification and should be adopted regardless, since it also covers destination coverage, manifest-driven object counts, and independent output validation that the engine never performs.
